title: Spiritual Tourism in Gujarat: Somnath, Dwarka, Ambaji and Jain Tirthas

description: A guide to spiritual tourism in Gujarat: the Jyotirlingas of Somnath and Nageshwar, Dwarkadhish and Bet Dwarka, the Shakti shrines of Ambaji and Pavagadh, Dakor and Akshardham, the Jain hills of Palitana and Girnar, Sabarmati Ashram, festivals such as Navratri, a Saurashtra temple route and seasons.
dek: Gujarat combines two Jyotirlingas, one of the four dhams, major Shakti shrines and the holiest Jain hills.

intro: Gujarat's Saurashtra coast holds Somnath, the first of the twelve Jyotirlingas, and Dwarka, one of the four dhams and the city of Krishna, with the Nageshwar Jyotirlinga nearby. Inland are two of Gujarat's most visited Devi shrines, Ambaji and Pavagadh, and the Krishna temple at Dakor.
The state is also central to Jainism, with the temple hills of Shatrunjaya at Palitana and Girnar above Junagadh. Most sites are linked by good roads, making a temple road trip easy to plan.
quickAnswer: Gujarat's main spiritual destinations are Somnath and Nageshwar (Jyotirlingas), Dwarkadhish Temple and Bet Dwarka, the Devi shrines of Ambaji and Pavagadh, Dakor, and the Jain hills of Palitana and Girnar. A Saurashtra temple route from Ahmedabad covering Dwarka, Somnath, Junagadh and Palitana takes about seven to eight days. October to March is the best time.
takeaways: Somnath and Nageshwar are Jyotirlingas; Dwarka is one of the four dhams.
Ambaji and Pavagadh are major Devi shrines, both with ropeways.
Palitana and Girnar are among the most important Jain tirthas.
A Saurashtra temple route takes about a week by road.
Navratri, celebrated with garba across the state, is the biggest festival.

sections.heading: More to see
list: Akshardham in Gandhinagar, a large Swaminarayan temple complex.
Sabarmati Ashram in Ahmedabad, Gandhi's home from 1917 to 1930.
The Modhera Sun Temple, an 11th-century monument.
Bahucharaji, a Devi shrine in Mehsana district.

sections.heading: Where to stay
list: Dwarka and Somnath: hotels, temple-trust guesthouses and dharamshalas close to the temples.
Palitana: dharamshalas run by Jain trusts and simple hotels near the foot of the hill.
Junagadh: hotels in the old city for Girnar.
Ahmedabad: the widest choice, and a good base for Dakor, Ambaji and Pavagadh.

sections.heading: Tips
list: Start early each day; Saurashtra afternoons are hot for much of the year.
Dress codes are relaxed at most temples, but modest clothing is expected.
Book trains to Dwarka and Somnath early for Diwali and Janmashtami.
Gujarat is a dry state; alcohol is not served in most hotels.

sections.heading: When to go
list: October to March: pleasant weather for temple visits and climbs.
Navratri (September or October): garba across the state and crowds at Ambaji and Pavagadh.
Janmashtami: large celebrations at Dwarka and Dakor.
April to June: very hot in Saurashtra; climb Palitana and Girnar at dawn.

safety: Darshan waits vary from minutes to many hours; no one can guarantee quick darshan, so plan buffer time.
Dress modestly and follow each place of worship's rules on dress, phones and photography.
Start the Palitana and Girnar climbs early and carry water.
Check ropeway status before planning Ambaji, Pavagadh and Girnar visits.

faqs.q: How many days are needed for a Gujarat temple tour?
faqs.a: About seven to eight days for Dwarka, Somnath, Junagadh and Palitana.
Ambaji is widely revered as a Shakti Peetha, though counts and lists differ between traditions.

faqs.q: What is the best time to visit Gujarat's temples?
Where can I see Navratri garba in Gujarat?
faqs.a: Across the state, with large public events in Ahmedabad and Vadodara; Ambaji and Pavagadh draw big crowds of pilgrims.

faqs.q: How do I get to Palitana?
faqs.a: By road from Bhavnagar (about 50 km) or Ahmedabad (about 215 km).

faqs.q: Can I combine a Gir safari with Somnath?
faqs.a: Yes. Sasan Gir is about 45 km from Somnath.
